newsitem.title: USA: Applied Materials third-quarter earnings surge.
newsitem.headline: Applied Materials third-quarter earnings surge.

text.p: Applied Materials Inc. said Tuesday its fiscal third-quarter profit surged 42 percent, far better than Wall Street expected, on strong sales of a new generation of semiconductor factory equipment.

Applied Materials, whose earnings reflect the expected health of the semiconductor industry in coming quarters, said its profit from operations rose to $145.2 million, or 77 cents a share, from $102.1 million, or 54 cents, in the same quarter a year ago.
Wall Street expected the biggest manufacturer of chip making equipment to report profit from operations of 68 cents a share, according to a recent analyst survey by research service First Call Corp.
The better-than-expected results boosted Applied Materials' stock as high as $92 in after-hours trading. The stock had closed up 75 cents at $90.25 for the day.

Applied Materials is the biggest manufacturer of semiconductor processing and chip making equipment. Because semiconductor companies place orders for its products in anticipation of higher production in coming quarters, Applied Materials' results often serve as a barometer of the semiconductor industry's growth six months out.
Many of its customers are placing orders for products that can manufacturer higher-capacity memory chips and faster microprocessors, Applied Materials said.
"In addition, we have seen orders accelerating for leading-edge foundry capacity investment in the Asia-Pacific region," said Chairman James Morgan.

Applied also unveiled several large orders. The company said White Oak Semiconductor, a joint venture between Siemens Electronics and Motorola Inc., ordered processing gear worth more than $100 million.
Revenue for the quarter ended July 27 declined 5.2 percent to $1.06 billion from $1.12 billion a year ago.
With an $80 million gain from a lawsuit settlement and a bad debt expense of $16.3 million, the company had net income of $186.6 million, or 98 cents, in the most recent quarter.
The company also said it booked new orders of $1.24 billion, up 22 perent from $1.01 billion in the second quarter. Backlog rose to $1.65 billion at the end of the third quarter.
